answer: A 511 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the comet index keeps every digest, the meadow audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, because the lagoon fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 27 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
